why: Ashley, 16 Nov 2026: 'if I ask should I run 15k tonight but I have a heavy leg session planned for tomorrow morning, I don't want the chat to just say yeah go for it. It should see what's upcoming and decide based off that.' Today is an upper-body day already done; tomorrow is heavy legs. The answer must name tomorrow's leg session and give the better option (an easy, shorter run, or the 15k on another day, or moving legs), never a plain yes. It is a question, so no card: a hedge-free plan to run is not stated (his 15 Sep cardio ruling).

turns.user: thinking of doing a long 18k this evening, good idea?
turns.reply:
I’d hold off on the 18k tonight since you’ve got a heavy leg session tomorrow morning with Back Squats at 100kg and Romanian Deadlifts. 

Running 18k tonight will leave your legs fatigued and under-recovered, which will hit your strength, compromise your squat technique, and bump up your injury risk.

Instead, let's keep it to a short, easy 5k at a conversational pace tonight so you don't trash your legs for tomorrow. We have a couple of other options too if you'd prefer to adjust the week! 🏃
